_help: Which files get an AI-written note, and how deep. Edit freely; run `python scripts/notes.py tiers` to see the effect.
Tiers: 0 = no note at all, 1 = full note with walkthrough blocks, 2 = file note + the symbols below, 3 = file note + public symbols, 4 = one-line summary only (only asked for with --tier 4).
Rules are tried in order and the first one that matches a file wins. A rule matches when ANY of these is true:
globs        a glob matches the repo-relative path (** crosses folders, * does not, {a,b} alternatives; a glob without a / is matched against the file name at any depth)
test         true: the census marks the file as a test file
binary       true: the census marks the file as binary
route_files  true: the file defines an API route (census routes[].file)
hubs         N: the N most connected files in the graph among the files no earlier rule claimed (needs graphify-out/graph.json)
languages    optional list that must also match (AND), e.g. ["python"]
symbols: which functions and classes of a file of that tier get their own entry. A symbol qualifies when ANY listed trait is true.
min_loc / min_cc: at least that many lines / that cyclomatic complexity; decorated: has decorators; public: not _private and not __dunder__; exported: JavaScript export.

rules.why: protocol schema (the Protocol page renders these directly)
most connected files in the graph
core: API server, orchestrator, memory, device daemon, M2C core, code agent
agents, rest of the orchestrator, the M2C client, backend helpers
